title: Class Field Theory
summary: Class field theory describes abelian field extensions through the arithmetic of the base field. This library formalizes its local and global forms for local fields, number fields and function fields.
overview: Class field theory classifies finite Galois extensions with abelian Galois group using arithmetic data of the base field. Local reciprocity uses the field’s multiplicative group; global reciprocity uses ideal classes or idèle classes, which combine information from all places. The theory grew out of reciprocity laws and the work of Kronecker, Weber, Hilbert and Takagi; Artin’s reciprocity law of 1927 connects the classification with the splitting of primes.

This library formalizes local class field theory for nonarchimedean local fields and global class field theory for both number fields and function fields over finite fields. It develops the Artin maps, norm subgroups and existence theorems that give these classifications, together with their ramification and cohomological foundations. The main references are Serre’s [Local Fields](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4757-5673-9) and Milne’s [Class Field Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/CFT.pdf) and [Arithmetic Duality Theorems](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ADTnot.pdf).
scopeNote: The selection covers local fields, number fields, and global function fields over finite fields. The function-field existence theorem uses the ordinary idèle-class topology. The selected local-field reciprocity theorem asserts existence.

entries.title: Local class field theory: reciprocity and existence
entries.summary: Finite abelian extensions of a local field correspond to open subgroups of finite index in its multiplicative group, with Galois groups given by the corresponding norm quotients.
statement: Let $K$ be a nonarchimedean local field, with its valuative topology, and let $L/K$ be a finite abelian Galois extension. There exists a continuous surjective homomorphism
$$\operatorname{Art}_{L/K}:K^\times\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(L/K),\qquad \ker(\operatorname{Art}_{L/K})=N_{L/K}(L^\times).$$
Here $N_{L/K}(L^\times)$ is the subgroup of field norms.
For a nonarchimedean local field $K$, let $\widehat{K^\times}_{\mathrm{top}}$ be the inverse limit of $K^\times/U$ over open normal subgroups $U$ of finite index. Then
$$\widehat{K^\times}_{\mathrm{top}}\ \simeq_{\mathrm{top}}\ G_K^{\mathrm{ab}},\qquad G_K=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K).$$
The right side is the topological abelianization: the quotient by the closure of the commutator subgroup.
Fix a nonarchimedean local field $K$ and a separable closure. Finite abelian intermediate extensions correspond to open finite-index subgroups of $K^\times$ through
$$L\longmapsto N_{L/K}(L^\times).$$
The correspondence reverses inclusion: $L_1\subseteq L_2$ exactly when $N_{L_2/K}(L_2^\times)\subseteq N_{L_1/K}(L_1^\times)$.
history: Serre's Local Fields presents the cohomological approach to local reciprocity, following the development associated with Hochschild and Artin–Tate. This finite quotient formulation is a convenient point of entry to that theory.

Lubin and Tate's 1965 paper supplies an explicit formal-group perspective on local abelian extensions. Serre's cohomological presentation gives a complementary route to the reciprocity theorem assembled here at the profinite level.

The existence theorem complements reciprocity in classical local class field theory. Lubin–Tate theory provides explicit local abelian extensions, while Serre treats existence together with local symbols in the final part of Local Fields.

entries.title: Number fields: global Artin reciprocity
entries.summary: Ray class reciprocity describes Frobenius in finite abelian extensions; idelic reciprocity identifies the abelianized absolute Galois group.
statement: Let $L/K$ be a finite abelian extension of number fields. There are a modulus $\mathfrak m$ and a surjective homomorphism
$$\operatorname{Art}_{L/K,\mathfrak m}:\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}(K)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(L/K).$$
Here $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}(K)$ is the ray class group of modulus $\mathfrak m$.

The extension is unramified away from $\mathfrak m$. For a finite prime $\mathfrak p$ outside its finite support and a prime $\mathfrak P$ above $\mathfrak p$, the map sends $[\mathfrak p]$ to the arithmetic Frobenius at $\mathfrak P$.
Let $K$ be a number field, $\mathbb A_K^\times$ its idèle group, and $C_K=\mathbb A_K^\times/K^\times$ its idèle class group. Write $C_K^0$ for the connected component of the identity. Then
$$C_K/C_K^0\ \simeq_{\mathrm{top}}\ G_K^{\mathrm{ab}}.$$
Here $G_K=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K)$, and $G_K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ denotes its topological abelianization.
history: Artin's 1927 reciprocity map made the correspondence with Galois groups canonical through Frobenius. Milne's historical discussion explains the earlier contributions of Kronecker, Weber, Hilbert, and Takagi to the class-field correspondence.

Milne's notes explain the algebraic and cohomological approach associated with Chevalley and Artin–Tate and present both ideal-theoretic and idelic reciprocity. The idelic formulation unifies finite-place and infinite-place conditions.

entries.title: Function fields: global reciprocity and class-field existence
entries.summary: Open subgroups of finite index in the ordinary idèle class group classify finite abelian extensions, and completion gives absolute reciprocity.
statement: Let $k$ be a finite field and $K/k$ a function field finite over a chosen $k(t)$. Write $C_K=\mathbb A_K^\times/K^\times$ with its ordinary quotient topology. Every open subgroup $H\subseteq C_K$ of finite index is exactly $N_{L/K}(C_L)$ for a unique finite abelian extension $L/K$ inside a fixed separable closure.
The actual norm map supplies an inclusion-reversing equivalence $L\longmapsto N_{L/K}(C_L)$. The constructed finite Artin map and the completed absolute Artin map give
$$C_K/N_{L/K}(C_L)\simeq\operatorname{Gal}(L/K),\qquad \widehat{C_K}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_K^{\mathrm{ab}}.$$
The completion uses all ordinary open subgroups of finite index, and the second isomorphism is an isomorphism of topological groups extending the constructed absolute Artin map.

The Lean interface uses principal-divisor data: every nonzero function has a finitely supported divisor of valuation orders and degree zero. The library constructs these data from the function-field structure over the finite base field, and for its finite extensions.
history: Function-field class field theory expresses abelian covering data through idèles and their norm groups. Milne’s Chapter I, Appendix A develops its local and global reciprocity formulations.

entries.title: Local fields: the Hasse–Arf theorem
entries.summary: Upper ramification breaks of a finite abelian local extension are integral.
statement: Let $L/K$ be a finite abelian extension of nonarchimedean local fields, with compatible valuations. Let $G_i$ be the lower ramification groups, and put
$$\varphi(n)=\frac{1}{|G_0|}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|G_i|\quad(n\in\mathbb N).$$
If $G_n\ne G_{n+1}$, then $\varphi(n)\in\mathbb Z$. The formal statement gives an integer $z$ with the rational equality $\varphi(n)=z$.
history: Arf's original ramification paper appeared in volume 181 of Crelle's journal in 1940. Serre's Local Fields develops the ramification and norm theory in which the Hasse–Arf theorem is situated.

entries.title: Number fields: the cyclic Hasse norm theorem
entries.summary: For a cyclic number-field extension, local norm equations have a global solution.
statement: Let $L/K$ be a finite cyclic Galois extension of number fields and let $a\in K^\times$. Then
$$a\in N_{L/K}(L^\times)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\in N_{L\otimes_K K_v\,/\,K_v}\bigl((L\otimes_K K_v)^\times\bigr)\ \text{for every place }v.$$
The right side includes every finite and every infinite completion. The norm after base change is the determinant norm of the resulting finite algebra.
history: The Hasse norm theorem is a central example of a local-to-global principle. Milne treats it through cyclic cohomology and idèle classes and explains why the corresponding assertion fails for general noncyclic extensions.

entries.title: Number fields: the Kronecker–Weber theorem
entries.summary: Every finite abelian extension of the rational numbers embeds into a cyclotomic field.
statement: Every finite abelian extension $L/\mathbb Q$ is contained in a cyclotomic field. More precisely, there exist an integer $n>0$ and a $\mathbb Q$-algebra embedding
$$L\hookrightarrow\mathbb Q(\zeta_n),$$
where $\zeta_n$ is a primitive $n$th root of unity.
history: Milne records Hilbert's 1896 proof following earlier incomplete proofs by Kronecker and Weber. The theorem is the rational-number-field prototype for the broader problem of explicitly generating abelian extensions.
